penetration_label: Significant -- Huawei is an active core RAN/5G partner, alongside diversified vendors
source_name: Developing Telecoms -- Huawei and e& UAE partner for energy-saving 5G performance
rationale: e& UAE deployed Huawei's dual-band 64T64R MetaAAU radio unit on its live 5G network. UAE is simultaneously the most US-integrated Gulf state on chips, illustrating a hedging pattern rather than exclusive alignment.

penetration_label: Significant -- Huawei is STC's lead vendor for advanced 5G features, alongside Nokia and Ericsson
source_name: Gulf Business -- stc, Huawei deploy Saudi Arabia's first Full Duplex network; Mobile World Live -- stc Group and Huawei Launch SuperLink
rationale: STC (Saudi Telecom Company) runs a three-vendor 5G network with Nokia, Huawei, and Ericsson, but Huawei is specifically the lead partner for STC's headline advanced-feature launches -- the SuperLink service (commercially launched Nov 2024) and Saudi Arabia's first Full Duplex deployment (2026), plus an earlier Huawei managed-services deal. This is a genuinely mixed-vendor picture like Qatar's, but with Huawei carrying more of STC's cutting-edge feature rollouts specifically. Notably this sits in telecom RAN/core infrastructure, a different domain from Saudi Arabia's aggressive US-chip pivot on the AI-compute side via HUMAIN -- the two data points (telecom vendor mix vs. AI compute sourcing) are not in tension, they're just about different technology layers.

penetration_label: Moderate -- mixed-vendor 5G core (Nokia core, Huawei RAN/partnership elements)
source_name: RCR Wireless -- Ooredoo partners with Huawei to transition to 5.5G
rationale: Ooredoo Qatar uses Nokia technology for its 5G cloud-native core network and has also trialed Ericsson equipment, while separately holding a Huawei 5.5G/core-modernization partnership -- a genuinely mixed vendor picture, scored lower than peers where Huawei is clearly the primary vendor.

penetration_label: Moderate -- Batelco's current 5G expansion uses Ericsson; Huawei only in early-stage 6G talks
source_name: AGBI -- Batelco in talks to trial 6G technology in Bahrain
rationale: Bahrain's national operator Batelco has tapped Ericsson to expand its current-generation 5G coverage, while separately holding only tentative, unconfirmed talks with Nokia, Huawei, and Ericsson about 6G trials (R&D-stage, expected rollout not before the 2030s per Batelco's own CEO as of this source). This is Bahrain-specific sourcing (an improvement on the prior regional-only citation), and it points toward a lower penetration score than initially scored: Huawei is one of three vendors in early-stage talks, not Bahrain's current deployed 5G vendor.

penetration_label: Deep -- Huawei is core 5G-A vendor across all three major operators
source_name: RCR Wireless -- Kuwait deploys 5G-A with Huawei and Knetco
rationale: Kuwait's 2025 5G-A rollout involved Huawei, Knetco and Kuwait's telecom regulator CITRA working with all three national operators (Ooredoo, Zain, stc) -- the most concretely documented multi-operator Huawei relationship of the GCC states covered here.

penetration_label: Significant -- Ooredoo Group's regional Huawei 5G partnership covers Oman
source_name: RCR Wireless -- Huawei to boost Ooredoo's 5G operations in four markets
rationale: Ooredoo Group's Huawei 5G/5G-A partnership explicitly spans Oman alongside Qatar and Kuwait, per a 2024 MWC agreement covering core-network modernization across Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq, Tunisia, Algeria and the Maldives.

penetration_label: Deep -- Huawei entrenched since 1998, central to CPEC digital infrastructure
source_name: Newswire.pk -- Huawei, Transworld launch Pakistan's first 400G network to boost CPEC's digital backbone
rationale: Huawei has operated in Pakistan since 1998 with roughly 1,600 employees (91% Pakistani nationals) and in Nov 2025 helped deploy Pakistan's first 400G optical backbone along CPEC routes with Transworld Associates; Pakistan's telecom regulator (PTA) also signed a 2025 capacity-building MOU with Huawei.

penetration_label: Deep -- multi-decade core-network partnership with Turkcell continuing through 2025
source_name: TechAfrica News -- Huawei and Turkcell Join Forces to Build Turkiye's Smart, Sustainable 5G-A Future
rationale: Turkcell and Huawei have partnered on RAN and all-cloud core network buildouts since at least 2015-2019 and renewed 5G-A/quantum-secure-network MOUs at MWC 2024 and MWC 2025. Read alongside Turkey's 2020 CAATSA sanctioning over its Russian S-400 purchase, this reflects a broader pattern of hedging beyond the Western bloc rather than an isolated telecom-vendor choice.

penetration_label: No significant Chinese ICT vendor presence in core telecom infrastructure
source_name: Mobile World Live -- 'US confident on Israel Huawei, ZTE ban'; INSS -- 'The 5G Tender in Israel and the Global Struggle against Huawei'
rationale: Under direct US pressure (Trump reportedly warned Netanyahu in March 2019 that a Huawei/ZTE 5G deal would curtail security cooperation), Israel's security establishment structurally excluded Huawei and ZTE from its telecom infrastructure tenders. Huawei retains only R&D/talent-employment operations in Israel (development centers, not network vendor contracts) -- there is no core-RAN, core-network, or major-carrier vendor relationship, unlike the Gulf states in the existing dataset.

penetration_label: Significant -- Huawei is a core RAN vendor for at least one major carrier, plus an active cloud region, with a live bid to expand into national AI infrastructure
source_name: Telecom Review Africa -- 'Orange Teams Up with Huawei for 5G Rollout in Egypt'; Huawei -- 'Huawei Cloud Goes Live in Egypt'
rationale: Huawei supplies Orange Egypt's Massive MIMO RAN equipment and has an infrastructure partnership with Telecom Egypt, while Vodafone/e& Egypt lean more on Ericsson/Nokia -- a genuinely mixed-vendor market, similar to Saudi Arabia's scored pattern. Beyond telecom, Huawei launched a $300m/5-year Huawei Cloud 'Egypt Region' on 21 May 2024 (Cairo hub for North Africa), and in Aug 2026 bid (with blacklisted partner iFlytek) to build Egypt's national AI training/inference data center -- not yet awarded, so not scored 'deep' (4) on that basis alone, but noted as an active escalation vector.

penetration_label: Minimal/isolated -- legacy 2G/3G/4G Huawei backbone, but government security services barred Huawei/ZTE from 5G bidding and both major operators chose non-Chinese 5G vendors
source_name: TahawulTech -- 'Jordan government will secretly restrict Chinese companies from building 5G networks'; Nokia press release -- 'Nokia selected by Zain Jordan for nationwide 5G'
rationale: Huawei built Jordan's 2G/3G/4G backbone historically, but Jordan's General Intelligence Directorate warned telecom operators against including Huawei/ZTE in 5G bidding (citing a 2021 NATO-linked security assessment), and following a Sept 2022 TRC stimulus package both major operators picked non-Chinese vendors for 5G: Zain selected Nokia (announced 8 Apr 2023) and Umniah selected Ericsson. Scored above 0 only because of the still-present legacy-generation Huawei infrastructure footprint; scored well below the Gulf peers where Huawei holds an active current-generation RAN role.

penetration_label: Deep -- Huawei historically dominant across Iraq's telecom sector, core 20+-year partner for Asiacell, expanding into enterprise/cloud via a 2025 China Mobile International tie-up
source_name: The Wire China -- 'Huawei: The Iraq Years' (Jan 2025); Iraq Business News -- Asiacell and China Mobile International Partner to Accelerate Iraq's Digital Transformation (June 2025)
rationale: A former US State Department advisor is quoted saying Huawei effectively 'owned' Iraq's telecom sector, citing over 600 contracts worth billions of dollars since the 2000s, including a 20-year core partnership with Asiacell (Iraq's largest operator) that in 2023 explicitly extended into integrating AI into Iraq's telecom services. On 2 June 2025, Asiacell signed a further MoU with China Mobile International to jointly deliver enterprise/B2B digital solutions, extending the relationship beyond RAN into cloud/enterprise. Counterweight: Iraq's flagship national 5G license was awarded to Vodafone in late 2025, and Zain Iraq's Kurdistan network-modernization Huawei deal ($46m) dates to 2019 -- not an uncontested Huawei monopoly today, hence 4 rather than 5.

penetration_label: Moderate -- mixed-vendor picture: Touch uses Huawei alongside Nokia for LTE/5G, while Alfa (Lebanon's other major operator) uses only Nokia/Ericsson
source_name: TelecomDrive -- Lebanon's touch Selects Huawei for Bringing 5G; Capacity Media / SAMENA Daily News -- Alfa to upgrade Lebanon network to 4.5G with Nokia and Ericsson
rationale: Lebanon's two state-backed mobile operators split on vendor: Touch signed 4.5G LTE-Advanced agreements with both Huawei and Nokia and ran Lebanon's first commercial 5G trial (2018) on Huawei equipment, continuing into the 2024-2025 5G rollout (150 base stations, Huawei + Nokia). Alfa (managed by Orascom Telecom), by contrast, signed its 4.5G and 5G-readiness deals exclusively with Nokia and Ericsson. This even split across Lebanon's two operators, with Huawei present but non-exclusive even at Touch, supports a 'moderate/mixed' score comparable to Qatar's and Bahrain's.

penetration_label: Deep -- Huawei and ZTE together reported to control the majority of network infrastructure at Syria's two established mobile operators
source_name: Syrian Future Current (Tayyar al-Mustaqbal al-Souri) -- Digitalization and Cybersecurity in the New Syria (Feb 2026)
rationale: A February 2026 Syrian policy-institute analysis of the post-Assad telecom/cybersecurity landscape states that Huawei, and to a lesser extent ZTE, control more than 50% of the network infrastructure of Syria's two main operators, Syriatel and MTN Syria. Consistent with a long-running Huawei/ZTE presence predating the 2024 transition, but not fully independently corroborated -- a 2022 OCCRP investigation into a third, smaller operator (Wafa Telecom) found Iran-linked ownership but could not confirm Huawei/ZTE equipment supply (both denied it), and predates the change of government. Medium confidence because this rests on a single, specific, dated but non-mainstream source rather than a corroborating second outlet.

penetration_label: Deep -- Huawei/ZTE embedded across core telecom, broadband buildout, and national surveillance/censorship infrastructure, evading sanctions for over a decade
source_name: National Security News -- IRGC commander runs MTN-Irancell as Iran's internet goes dark (Feb 2026); Iran International -- Leaked Document Reveals Iran's Multiple Telecom Deals With China (May 2023)
rationale: A Huawei-built internet 'kill switch' project, press-estimated at $700M-$1B, is reported (Feb 2026) to be in its final stages at a fortified data center near Tehran, run through IRGC-controlled MTN Irancell (Iran's #2 carrier, ~56M subscribers) -- Huawei has separately confirmed selling Irancell network equipment. A 2023 leaked Ministry of ICT document additionally shows roughly ten separate China-Iran contracts spanning landline, 4G/5G broadband, satellite, and smartphone/messenger projects, including a ZTE-TCI $130.6M surveillance system for TCI (Iran's largest fixed operator). This is deep, multi-domain, sanctions-evading penetration, though I could not confirm a single current source stating Huawei is the primary RAN vendor for MCI/Hamrah-e-Aval (Iran's largest mobile operator, where Nokia has also historically supplied equipment) -- hence 4 rather than 5.

penetration_label: Moderate -- legacy Huawei/ZTE equipment in Yemen Mobile's network plus a Huawei-built, Huawei-operated ISP (AdenNet) in government-controlled Aden, but no confirmed major new deals since the war intensified
source_name: Yemen Mobile (Wikipedia, sourced to industry reporting); Barran Press -- Yemen's Ministry of Communications Launches Phase Two of AdenNet Expansion
rationale: Yemen Mobile's original CDMA network was Huawei-equipped, with ZTE and LG-Nortel equipment added in parts of the network historically. Separately, a USD 93M Huawei-built AdenNet system (funded via UAE backing, using Saudi Telecom fiber transit) went live in 2018 under the internationally recognized government, with Huawei remaining AdenNet's turnkey partner and a Phase Two expansion announced by Yemen's Ministry of Communications in November 2024. This is real but dated/isolated penetration relative to peers with confirmed current core-RAN Huawei contracts (e.g. Kuwait, Turkey) -- no evidence of a major new Huawei/ZTE deal was found since the conflict escalated, and the $93M AdenNet cost figure traces to secondary aggregation rather than a single primary contract document, so this is scored moderate with Medium rather than High confidence.

penetration_label: Minimal -- legacy ZTE/Huawei-built 2G/3G network infrastructure from the pre-2021 government era; 2023 Taliban-Huawei surveillance talks reported but no signed contract or deployment confirmed
source_name: Afghanistan Ministry of Communications and IT (mcit.gov.af) -- Afghan Telecom Signs Agreement of GSM and 3G Equipment with ZTE Company; DataCenterDynamics -- The Taliban reportedly meets with Huawei over Afghanistan surveillance plan
rationale: State-owned Afghan Telecom's 2G/3G network is roughly 70% ZTE-equipment and 30% Huawei-equipment per Ministry-era reporting, stemming from a ~$32M ZTE GSM/3G equipment contract (circa 2008) and a separate 2006 ZTE fiber-optic contract -- legacy infrastructure predating the Taliban's 2021 return to power. In August 2023, Taliban Interior Ministry officials met Huawei representatives in Kabul reportedly to discuss activating a nationwide advanced camera/surveillance system; Huawei denied firm plans, and no contract or deployment has been confirmed in subsequent reporting through this research pass. Scored 1 (minimal/isolated) to reflect that the confirmed penetration is dated legacy network hardware, not an active current deployment; the 2023 surveillance talks are flagged as reported but unconfirmed, not counted toward a higher score.
